messages:
Carlos M.: Hey folks, first week here. I followed README and started docker-compose but my app on host can't connect to Postgres in the stack. Error: 'could not connect to server: No such file or directory'. Using DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:dev@db:5432/appdb and bind mounting ./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data. What did I miss?

Ivy Chen: welcome! :wave: That DSN uses 'db' which is a container hostname. If your app runs on host you need to expose the port and use localhost (or 127.0.0.1). Either publish ports in compose: 
```yaml
ports:
  - "127.0.0.1:5432:5432"
```
or run the app as a service in the same compose project and keep using 'db'.

Carlos M.: aha I copied the env from the service example. If I publish port, is bind mounting PGDATA on mac ok? I've read about re-inits and perms on M1.

Rajat Singh: named volume is the safest on mac. Bind mounts can trigger initdb because of uid/permission mismatches from osxfs. Our usual pattern: set PGDATA to a subdir and use a named volume: 
```yaml
environment:
  PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
volumes:
  - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
volumes:
  pgdata: {}
```
That avoids host filesystem ownership issues. If you absolutely need host files, mount only migrations: ./migrations:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d and keep PGDATA as a named volume.

Carlos M.: thanks! One more quick thing: sometimes I see 'could not translate host name "db"' when the app runs in container. Any tip?

Ivy Chen: that usually means the app container and db are not in the same compose network or different project name. Use the same compose file/project or specify networks. Also ensure you didn't accidentally set `network_mode: host` (Mac handles that differently).

infra-bot: Updated docs/setup.md -> "Local DB tips: use named volumes for PGDATA on macOS, publish ports for host-side apps, use service hostnames for intra-compose communication" (https://git.internal/redwood/docs/setup.md) :white_check_mark:

Carlos M.: great, switching to named volume and exposing 127.0.0.1:5432 for my host-run app. Appreciate the help! :raised_hands:
